diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assumption \ref{assum:4.1} and Lemma \ref{lem:4.9} imply that $F(t,\cdot;v^h(t,\cdot))$ is bounded and Lipschitz continuous.

issues.failure_explanation: The Barles-Souganidis localization asserts a sequence (t_{k_m},y_m)->(t,x) that nearly attains the supremum of v^{h_m}-phi, but the sup in (4.3-1) runs over all y in R^d while v^h is controlled only on the box: Lemmas 4.8 and 4.9 bound D^alpha v^h solely for x in (-R,R)^d, and outside the box v^h(t_k,y)=sum_j (A^{-1}v_k^h)_j Phi(y-x^{(j)}) can be estimated only through ||A^{-1}||_infty (Delta_2 x)^{-d}, which no assumption controls. Near-maximizers may therefore escape to the uncontrolled exterior or to infinity (phi is not coercive), so the asserted sequence is unsupported; consequently (4.4), the application of Lemma 4.11 at y_m, and c_m->0 are not established as written. The same root appears where the proof calls F(t,.;v^h(t,.)) bounded and Lipschitz and feeds it to Lemma 4.10, which requires a globally Lipschitz function on R^d: the derivative bounds behind that claim hold only on the box. (The sup is also taken over continuous times s in [0,T) although v^{h_m} is defined only at grid times.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take the sup in (4.3-1) over grid times and the box (-R,R)^d where Lemma 4.9 applies; use the standard reduction to a coercive test function (modify phi only outside a neighborhood of (t,x)) so near-maximizers stay in a fixed compact set; and apply Lemma 4.10 to a globally Lipschitz extension of F(t_{k_m+1},.;v^{h_m}(t_{k_m+1},.)) from the box (e.g., via projection onto the box, which leaves the trace on Gamma, hence I(.), unchanged). The theorem's statement, hypotheses, and scope are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: Both the subsolution half of the proof of Theorem 4.5 and, symmetrically, the supersolution half are incomplete: existence of the localizing sequence and the convergence J_m->0 are unsupported as written, so the main convergence claim is unproven until the localization is repaired.
issues.title: Theorem 4.5's localization uses global control of v^h that is only established inside (-R,R)^d
issues.why_classification: More than a short local fix: the localization step must be rebuilt using several standard devices (sup restriction, coercive test function, extension for the J_m step). The repair is contained in the localization argument, needs no new nontrivial lemma or changed hypothesis, and loses no content, so it is not serious.

Then, considering $p=p_0$ and $\gamma=\gamma_0$, we find that

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 4.11 is stated only for C^3 functions whose derivatives up to order 3 are bounded by C_1, ensuring (D phi(x), D^2 phi(x)) lies in D; its lower one-sided bound is proved precisely by inserting (p,gamma)=(D phi(x),D^2 phi(x)). The viscosity test function phi is arbitrary C^3, so (D phi(y_m),D^2 phi(y_m)) need not lie in D and the lemma as stated does not apply to it. Only the upper one-sided bound (the third inequality of the chain) is actually needed, and that direction does follow from the same argument with phi-dependent constants, but as written the step invokes a result outside its hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: we apply Lemma \ref{lem:4.11} for the family $\{v^{h_m}(t_{k_m+1},\cdot), \varphi(t_{k_m+1},\cdot)\}_{m\ge 1}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Lemma 4.11 as two one-sided estimates, noting that the upper bound holds for any C^3 function with C, delta_1 depending on its C^3 norm; cite the two-sided version for v^{h_m} and only the upper one-sided version for phi. No conclusion changes.
issues.overall_effect: The third inequality of the central chain in the proof of Theorem 4.5 is formally unsupported.
issues.title: Lemma 4.11 is applied to the viscosity test function although it violates the lemma's derivative-bound hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Contained restatement fully justified by the lemma's own (appended) proof; the needed bound survives with no loss of content.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound available from (4.4) carries the tolerance (Delta t)_m^{3/2}, but the chain uses delta_m^{3/2} with delta_m = t_{k_m+1}-t_{k_m} <= (Delta t)_m; since the tolerance shrinks, the replacement goes in the wrong direction. Only Delta t -> 0 is assumed and arbitrary time grids are admitted, so delta_m can be far smaller than (Delta t)_m (e.g., a grid with one step of size (Delta t)^2); after the final division by delta_m the error term (Delta t)_m^{3/2}/delta_m can diverge instead of vanishing, so the closing o(1) estimate fails for grids the theorem allows.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose the near-maximizer tolerance in (4.3-1) as (min_k (t_{k+1}-t_k))^{3/2} instead of (Delta t)_m^{3/2}; then the tolerance divided by delta_m is at most (min_k (t_{k+1}-t_k))^{1/2} -> 0 and every other step is unchanged (equivalently, add a quasi-uniformity assumption on the time grid).
issues.overall_effect: As written, the convergence proof covers only time grids with delta_m comparable to Delta t (e.g., quasi-uniform), not the general grids permitted by the theorem's statement.
issues.title: Tolerance (Delta t)^{3/2} is replaced by delta_m^{3/2}, which is invalid on non-quasi-uniform time grids
issues.why_classification: A one-line change of the tolerance repairs the inference with no new hypothesis, no new lemma, and no loss of scope or conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: For d >= 2 the cube (-R,R)^d is not contained in the ball {|x| <= R} (corners have norm up to R sqrt(d)), so zeta(./R) = 1 holds only on the inscribed ball, not on the whole box. Hence tilde u^eps = u^eps zeta(./R) differs from u^eps at corner collocation points x^{(j)} in Gamma and at corner evaluation points x; since I depends on the trace on Gamma, I(tilde u^eps)(x) != I(u^eps)(x) in general, and the displayed identity used to invoke (4.1) is false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose the cutoff with zeta = 1 on the cube [-1,1]^d (or on {|x| <= sqrt(d)}); then tilde u^eps = u^eps on (-R,R)^d, which contains Gamma, the bound ||tilde u^eps||_{H^kappa} <= C ||u||_{C^{0,1}} eps^{-kappa} R^{d/2} is unchanged, and the lemma's statement and rate are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma 4.10 contains a false identity for d >= 2, so the lemma (used for J_m -> 0 and for the terminal condition in Theorem 4.5) is not established as written, although the estimate itself survives.
issues.title: Cutoff in Lemma 4.10 equals 1 only on a ball, so the truncation identity fails on the cube for d >= 2
issues.why_classification: A standard local modification of the cutoff fixes the identity; the method, conclusion, rate, and scope of the lemma are all unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: take $\delta_1\in (0,1]$ such that $x+\sqrt{\delta}w\in\mathcal{O}$ for all $w\in\mathcal{X}_{\delta,\theta}$, and $\delta\le\delta_1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The sup-inf expression evaluates phi at x + sqrt(delta) w with |w| up to delta^{-theta}, i.e., at distance up to delta^{1/2-theta} from x. For x closer than that to the boundary of O, these points leave O, where the C^3 function phi is not even defined, so no single delta_1 can serve all x in the open set O. The appended proof confirms this: it chooses delta_1 so that x + sqrt(delta) w stays in O, a condition depending on dist(x, boundary of O). What is actually established is the estimate for x ranging over a compact subset of O (with delta_1 adapted to it), a materially weaker statement than the uniform one claimed.

failure_location.quote: there exist $\delta_1\in (0,\infty)$ and $\beta\in (0,\infty)$ such that for $(t,x,z)\in [0,T]\times \mathcal{O}\times\mathbb{R}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the lemma for phi defined on a neighborhood of the closure of O (or on all of R^d), or restrict the claim to x in a compact subset of O with delta_1 depending on that subset; the application in Theorem 4.5 needs only interior points, so no content is lost.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the lemma is ill-defined for x near the boundary of O and only the localized version is proved; Theorem 4.5 invokes the lemma (at interior points y_m -> x) and formally inherits the gap until the statement is corrected.
issues.title: Lemma 4.11 claims one delta_1 uniform over all x in O, but the proof needs delta_1 adapted to dist(x, boundary of O)
issues.why_classification: A local restatement of the lemma's quantifiers closes the gap; the application and all downstream conclusions survive unchanged.
